utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old were you then, that is, on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: About 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The 7th of November, 1977.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that morning, where were you? And we are speaking now for the time being of the 4th of February.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the morning of the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was in my flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were there, did something happen that morning or that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us slowly what happened.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was sitting in a room, and at a certain point in time, I heard an explosion. I could tell that it was near; the explosion was very loud. I knew that my brother was outside and I was worried about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that explosion happened?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the front side of the building, so opposite my building. It hit another building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It hit another building opposite your building. Can I understand that to mean across the road, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, from your building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this question was a leading question because the location was pointed out directly, and I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness had said it hit a building opposite his building. I was just clarifying what exactly he meant by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were worried about your brother. Was your brother in your apartment at the time when you heard this explosion?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't. I was worried about him because I thought that he was outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you do anything?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I had a look through the window and, down below, I could see some things. First of all, there was a loud noise. I looked out of the window. I saw people who were wounded and I couldn't see my brother. I was worried about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these people who were wounded? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: In the street. Some were screaming, yelling for help. They were wounded. They were panicking, quite simply panicking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which street was this?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there any particular activity going on in that street and in that area of that street that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the people were gathered in that area where you saw these injured people?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, it was well known, everyone knew this because humanitarian was distributed there. We didn't have any food at the time and the only source of food was the humanitarian aid that the international community distributed to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the humanitarian aid distributed?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: In our street. They were supposed to distribute it in the park in our street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said, "It was well known." Can you tell us a little more about that? Well known in the community that humanitarian aid was distributed there, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was well known, humanitarian aid would arrive and it had to be distributed. We didn't all receive it directly from representatives of the international community. It was distributed to certain communities and then these communities would decide who should obtain this aid, to whom it should be distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that what the people who were outside your apartment were gathered for?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: That was behind my building. Yes, the humanitarian aid was distributed behind my building and that is where they gathered for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You looked out your window. I think it is to the front of your building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw injured people. Did you see your brother there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I saw wounded people, but I didn't see my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything after that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I didn't see him, I went to the other side of the building because my flat has a view of both sides. So I went there to see whether everything was all right with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the other side of the building is at the back of your building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is the other side of the building, so the side that gives on the playground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see him at that side where the playground is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened, if anything, while you were there looking?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I went out to the balcony and the second shell fell on the playground then. And I was wounded by this shell, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was wounded in the right arm, above the elbow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people in the vicinity of this playground and, if so, did anything happen to them?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were people there and something did happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that, please.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The shell fell. I went out to the balcony and tried to see my brother. I saw quite a few people. The shell fell then. I was wounded in the right arm. There were quite a lot of people who were lying down. They were -- they had been wounded. They were dead. Quite a lot of humanitarian aid had been scattered around. There were canisters there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything after that?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left the building. I left my flat. I went to see where my brother was and I went to fetch help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where exactly you went to?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: At the entrance I met my brother, I saw my brother. He was all right. He had been with a friend of his in his flat so nothing had happened to him. I then went to the clinic in order to be given first aid. This clinic is near my building so it is a couple of entrances lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- as you came out of your building where you saw your brother, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I did, the people still panicking and screaming. Some were taken away to hospital. Immediately, there were several cars which were at the scene. And it is then that the third shell fell. I then went to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "the third shell fell," can you be a little bit more descriptive. What did you hear or see, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: A loud explosion could be heard. These were explosions. From the building, I could hear that it was very near, although I didn't see where it fell exactly. But I heard a loud explosion and that's why I knew that it was nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say approximately which direction it came from, was it behind or to the side of the building that you lived in, or to the back?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't fall on the street. It fell on the playground at the same spot -- well, not the same spot, but the same playground where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it by that that this third explosion fell behind the building that you lived in?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left, did you notice any damage to any building or area in front of your building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: On the ground floor of the building, across the road from the one in which I lived, there was a large hole there. A lot of damage had been caused, and I could see that this is where the first shell had fallen when I was in the flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the vicinity of this damaged area of the building, do you know what that area of the building was being used for?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was not really a mosque. I didn't go into those buildings, but I heard that they were used for the children. This is where children would go for religious education and in order to get them off the streets a bit because there was shelling all the time. There was sniper shots all the time. So it was more secure and it was for the sake of their education, too, because at the time the schools were not open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say whether or not any of the children were in the mosque that day -- I beg your pardon, were in that building that was used to accommodate them that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go in there but I assume that there were some children there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went -- you left the scene and went somewhere. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the clinic, where I was given first aid. And they then sent me to the hospital in Dobrinja for further treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were at the hospital in Dobrinja, did you see anybody who was injured in this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were quite a few people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that day, and I am speaking just about that day, what -- did any shell or any shells fall in the area where you lived before those three shells fell?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Were these shells, the three shells which you have just spoken about, were the first shells to fall in your area on that day or was there previous shelling before that on that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Shelling went on all the time, not just on that day, but all the time. But on that day, I don't think that there was any shelling during that period and at that location. There was no shelling at that location. No shells fell there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take it that you mean that no shells fell that day before the three which you describe?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think that this happened on that day at the same location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what the weather was like at the time when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Not very well, but I know that it wasn't raining.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know of any type of military activity that was being conducted on the street in front of your apartment that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By no means -- well, was any military activity being conducted on the street in front of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood the question very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you --

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: If you mean that -- if you want to know whether there was anyone fighting, no, there was nothing like that on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the playground behind your apartment, was there any military activity being conducted there that day or any soldiers there that day when the shelling occurred?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the district that you live at, in your neighbourhood, do you know of any military facility in the area?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that there was a small office that belonged to the army, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this small office?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the building across the road from the one in which I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us how small, or tell us what do you mean by "small office"? About how many military personnel would you see there from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was a small room. Before the war, it was something like a kiosk, something like that. And there were a few soldiers there occasionally. I don't know. I didn't really notice them and I wasn't interested in them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, take your time, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were treated at the hospital in Dobrinja. If you saw a copy of your medical record, would you be able to identify it?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, may I have tendered to the witness Exhibit P3367?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your name on that document?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date, do you see the date?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date you see there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The 4th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the top right of the document, do you see something written in hand that is not printed? Do you?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you make it out?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: "Massacre in Dobrinja."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President I just ask the witness to read that into evidence because I think that is one part of the document which does not appear on the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We get used to these kind of situations, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a copy of your medical record?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It could be taken back from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you admitted to the hospital or were you discharged that day?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was discharged on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us earlier in your testimony that you had lived in apartments which had been shelled and that you had been injured before by shelling. Can you recall the first time you were injured by shelling?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can; on the 24th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you then?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Dobrinja III at the time, in Trg Junaka Socijalistickog number 5. That is where I was living at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time of the day or night were you injured?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: In the daytime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened when you were injured?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: On that day I was on the balcony with my grandmother who was preparing breakfast. We didn't have any electricity. So it wasn't possible to cook, really, to cook in the house. So we improvised a grill which was on the balcony and we used wood for it, and this is where we would cook. My grandmother was preparing some food and I was standing by her. And we were there for a while and a shell then fell, a tank shell fell a metre or a metre and-a-half away from me, and it wounded me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did the shell explode?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you wounded on this occasion, what part of your body was wounded?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was my finger on my right hand and my right knee. Luckily, this was an armour-piercing tank shell so there wasn't too much shrapnel, and a fridge which was by my side also helped me. It obstructed some of the shrapnel. The remainder of the shell, the one that exploded, entered, it penetrated the building and destroyed the flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to your grandmother at that time?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No. Fortunately, nothing happened to her. She was crouching down behind a concrete wall. She was preparing some food, she was occupied with the grill, so the concrete protected her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly, or may I put it this way, on which floor of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. apartment were you at the time of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: On the fifth floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that balcony face any particular area or community?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It faces Gavrica Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say which party to the conflict controlled this area, Gavrica Brdo, at the time of your injury? That is, was it under the control of the army of Republika Srpska or under the control of the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The area was under the control of Republika Srpska. It was their land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your balcony or from the balcony that you were at with your grandmother, was there any obstruction between there and -- I am going to get the pronunciation wrong, but Gavrica Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No, not the area towards Gavrica Brdo. That is, there were some buildings located around the square. However, when looking from my balcony, the view of Gavrica Brdo was unobstructed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know of any tanks being at Gavrica Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I know that there were tanks for quite a while during the war and they were targeting Dobrinja most, but other parts of the town as well. They were visible with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say where that shell which injured you in October 1992 was fired from?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can say that it was fired from Gavrica Brdo. That was the only possible direction it could have come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you injured another time by a shelling before the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember the date of that incident?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The 13th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were you when you were injured at that time?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I happened to be in an apartment with my girlfriend. We were just sitting down in the apartment where some young people used to gather because it was impossible to be outside in the street. So we had to stick to the inside, to the apartments, because we were, to a certain extent, sheltered there from shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this apartment?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: In Dobrinja I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the address?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I think the name of the street was Jovan Veselinova, but it has been renamed into Zlatnih Ljiljana Square, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please repeat what he has just said? I think that the interpreters are not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as a general rule, if you would like the witness to do something, would you either address me or Mr. Stamp, so that he can -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I was addressing you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then perhaps not properly understand. You said, "Could the witness please repeat what he has just said." The line is such that it could be addressed both to the witness and to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] I am so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Hafizovic, could you please repeat the answer to the question whether you remember the address. That was about that part, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was the last name that the witness said. I don't think that everybody got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The beginning of your answer was, "I think the name of the street was Jovan Veselinova but it has been renamed into..." Could you please repeat the new name of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the new name of the street is Zlatnih Ljiljana Square or Trg Zlatnih Ljiljana. I believe that that is the new name of the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This building that you were at when you were injured in January 1993, how do you enter that building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you enter the building and leave the building, if you wanted to?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think the question has been properly interpreted, or I may have misunderstood it. Would you be so kind and repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the building from the front or from the back of the building? And that is the building that you were injured in on the 13th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The entrance was from the back, from some openings that had been made, because it was not possible to enter the apartment from the front, from the facade, because of the constant shooting. So we used this back entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were injured this time, on what storey of the building were you at with your girlfriend and the other young people?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was on the ground floor. So the apartment was located on the ground floor of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day or night was it, can you recall, that you were injured?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was already dark, so it must have been sometime between 8.00 and 9.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any --

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: 8.00 and 10.00. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any kind of lighting in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Here the transcript reads between 8.00 and 10.00. That is, I am not sure. I think that it was between 8.00 and 10.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine. We understand it is an estimate of the time. So, tell us, did you have any type of lighting inside the apartment at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, the witness said, this last sentence, "between 8.00 and 9.00."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no electricity during that period of time. Actually, for quite some time, we didn't have any electricity so we had to find ways to light up the room, and we used a gas lamp. We improvised some kind of gas light because there was gas pipeline in the building. And this is what we used for lighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us what happened at the time you were injured.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: We were sitting in this apartment, me and my girlfriend, and talking. At one point we heard a very loud explosion. She fell down on the floor and I lay down on top of her. The lights were gone as a result of the explosion, and after a while, we got up and I inquired whether anyone was injured in the dark. Everybody said that they were not. But I felt something warm on me and I realised that I was bleeding. I touched my head and realised that I was covered in blood. I didn't want to cause any panic. I didn't want to frighten my friends, so I ran out into the street. And since the lines were very close, I could hear them. Of course, at the same time, I was crying out for help but I also heard them talk, using some abusive language. And a man passed by and he took me to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you -- the place was not too far from the confrontation line and you heard "them" talk. Who did you hear?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers of Republika Srpska, if I am allowed to use this language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was said?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: They were laughing and they were saying something to the effect, "Hey, you Balijas, how many of you did we kill this time?" And something else but I don't remember anything else. I was frightened. After all, I had this wound on my head and I was scared. I didn't know what was going to happen to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this said in a normal tone of voice or was it shouted across the line?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: They were shouting. They were shouting, and that was not the first time. Whenever they did something of the sort and, see, the neighbourhood of Dobrinja is so structured that sometimes the separation line passed through a building or between two buildings. They were very close and they were trying to frighten us, to intimidate us and to humiliate us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to a hospital on this occasion when you suffered that injury to your head. Were you admitted on that occasion or were you discharged?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was discharged because there were many wounded people in this hospital. And the conditions were not much better than elsewhere. They didn't have electricity either. So I was released home for treatment at home. They treated my wound, put some stitches on it, and after that, they discharged me. They cleared up the wound and removed everything that was not part of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was very dangerous to go in front of that building because of the constant shooting. Can you recall any incident in which anybody had been shot in that vicinity?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Snipers were active in those streets. It was not safe to walk down the main street and we used to run from one building to another. Quite a few people were wounded during the conflict. There were many such cases. I once assisted a wounded person in one of these incidents, if that is what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, it is. The time when you assisted this wounded person, can you recall when this was?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, however, after my first wounding; I was still recovering from wounds. I mean I was still not able to walk normally. I was still in pain and my arm hurt. So it was during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your first wounding --

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this event in which you assisted this lady could have occurred approximately how long after this first wounding?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I am not sure about the exact date, but I know that I was still recovering from the wound, so I can conclude that it occurred sometime after the first time I was wounded. Maybe a month after that, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that it occurred before the second time you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure about that. I am sure that it was before I was wounded for the second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that the witness has just said that it was during his first wounding, that is, one month after the first wounding, and I don't think that the second wounding was -- took place one month after, after the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have expressed myself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in a not very clear manner. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... try to clarify the issue and see whether there is an issue and see whether it can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, Witness, that it was approximately a month after your first injury that you assisted this person. The second injury was on the 13th of January, 1993. So is it correct to say that the occasion when you assisted this person was between the time when you suffered the first injury and the time when you suffered the second injury?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, but I am not sure about the -- about the day, as I indicated, if you understand. If necessary, I can explain further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't expect you to be precise about every date. Thank you. I am going to enquire briefly into the circumstances in which you came to assist this girl. Tell us, this person, well, was it a girl, a boy, a man or a woman that you assisted?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was a girl whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct now, but at the beginning, Mr. Stamp -- Mr. Stamp has actually corrected his answer so I withdraw my remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: So it was a young woman, a girl. I don't think she was over 15. She was unknown to me. And she was crossing -- she was running across the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. She was actually running across the green part of the street, the lawn. And the area was somewhat lower than the rest of the street, but it was frequently targeted by a sniper. I don't know what happened. She must have bent or something and at that time she was hit by a sniper. But she was obviously still alive, although the sniper went on shooting, but nobody dared approach her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The sniper was shooting from where, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From the direction of Dobrinja I, which was under the control of Republika Srpska. This is the area from where fire was being opened for a long period of time during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When she was hit, what happened? Did she fall or did she continue running?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No, she fell down. She fell down and the sniper continued shooting. But, you know, whenever a person got wounded, others always tried to come to that person to help, but this was not possible because the shooting went on. And then I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that a little bit further. You said the shooting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. went on. Where was it being fired at, can you say?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The bullets were coming from the direction of Dobrinja I, that is, Republika Srpska, from where the view to the buildings in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street was unobstructed and that is where she was hit. There were several tracer bullets striking around her so we were able to see the direction from which they were coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So the shots were being fired by this sniper around her where she lay?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did this continue?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I couldn't tell you exactly how long it went on but I am sure it was at least for a couple of minutes. But nobody, as I said, dared approach her. The bullets were hitting the area around her and there was some dust coming from the ground where the bullets were impacting. So we realised that the shooting was going on, and nobody dared come to that girl and I -- since I had already been wounded, I remembered how I felt myself in the same situation. So after a brief period of time, I ran up to her and, of course, I was not able to pull her out alone but there was a man in the vicinity who finally also came to her and then the two of us pulled her out from this location. And as far as I know, she survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see this young -- this girl again?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I moved frequently in those days. But I heard that she was trying to find me, to thank me. I don't know. But I was not able to find her, nor was she.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am checking, Mr. President. And I am addressing you. I think that there has been a mistake in the record. I am reading the English transcript which says, "There was a man in the vicinity," and I thought I heard the witness say that there was a Bosnian soldier in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I did not hear what my friend has commented, but I think I know where that came from

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please clarify that, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say whether or not the person who helped you to pull this girl away was a Bosnian soldier?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I can say that it was a Bosnian soldier because I don't think that I would have been helped by a soldier from Republika Srpska there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just clarify, I don't think that he said earlier that a soldier assisted him, I think he said "a man." I think my friend has been referring to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wondered, as a matter of fact, why you were able to detect a possible source, and I would at least like to prevent, that would be to prevent that, on the basis of the witness statement, elements are introduced in the examination-in-chief by the Defence, just as I would not think it to be acceptable that the Prosecution would introduce elements in the examination-in-chief by the Defence later on, on the basis of written statements. So, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please tell me exactly where you thought you heard a Bosnian soldier to be pronounced, so that we can check in the original...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, are you asking me when I heard this or where in the transcript it can be found?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... at what time -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, to interrupt. Is it possible for me to add something because I see that you are having some problems. May I be allowed to provide the explanation? Mr. President, I am trying to locate the exact spot and I will tell you it is line 16, page 64, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since my computer was not connected in the beginning, I am a bit confused as far as pages are concerned. Could you please indicate the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] The time I read is -- I have no time, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your laptop -- well, Judge Nieto-Navia has a perfect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am sorry. Page 64, line 14, it says, "So after a brief period of time I run up to her and of course I was not able to pull her out alone, but there was a man in the vicinity who finally also came." It is 12.25.13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance. Did you, during your testimony just a while ago, did you tell us that it was a man in the vicinity or there was a Bosnian soldier in the vicinity? When for the first time asked, because later on you, upon another question by Mr. Stamp, you said it was a Bosnian soldier. But when you first mentioned the presence of a person who helped you, did you then say it was a man or did you say it was a Bosnian soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a man who was dressed in a uniform, a camouflage uniform. He may have been a soldier, or not. I don't know that. I don't know how much you know about it, but uniforms were sometimes donned by ordinary people, ordinary civilians, because there weren't no clothes that could be bought normally. So I don't know. But it was a man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was whether at first you testified that it was a man or that you testified that it was a Bosnian soldier. But at first, when you mentioned the presence of a person, did you say there was a man or did you say there was a Bosnian soldier? Or don't you remember? If you don't remember, it is no problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the interpreters can help, my colleague is telling me that it is possible that the witness said a Bosnian soldier. But since I didn't hear him clearly and could not ask him to clarify, I interpreted it as "a man."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have heard an explanation now from the interpreter's booth. I thank you very much for assisting us. I do understand that the English interpreters were not able to hear it perfectly well and therefore they translated "a man," where other colleagues have indicated that the witness would have said that it was a Bosnian soldier. So it seems that the issue has been clarified. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That is exactly what I wanted to say, that the witness said that it was a Bosnian soldier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that it must have been a problem of translation, rather, and so there is -- as far as I can see, there is no question about relying upon a written testimony during the examination, but it is just that the interpretation caused Mr. Piletta-Zanin to ask for a clarification because he heard "Bosnian soldier." Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, since we -- since it was interrupting anyhow, I even look at the clock very well, it is already past 12.30. How much time would you still need for your examination-in-chief, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would imagine probably 20 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we will now have a break. Mr. Hafizovic, we have to take a pause now and then, so we will have a break, that is for everyone, until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said this young girl was pulled by this man and yourself to safety. Was that after the firing stopped?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't shoot at us while we were trying to pull her out. Whether he -- he didn't shoot while we were pulling her out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how old was this young girl?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how old she was exactly, but she was young. I think she was about 17 or so. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was she dressed?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: She was wearing jeans and a T-shirt of some kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what part of her body was she injured?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: She was wounded in the face. So she had -- she was wounded in the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time? And I am asking particularly about the visibility at that time.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Visibility was good, I think. It was good. There was no rain. You could see well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time of day was this, did you say?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was it in the day or in the night when it was dark?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It was during the day, for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as this young girl lay there injured, for about how long did the sniper or snipers fire shots around her before they stopped?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: For a certain period of time. I don't know for how long exactly. I didn't have a look at my watch. But for a few minutes, I think. Long enough to notice that they had fired several shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June 2001, that is June last year, were you interviewed by an investigator of the -- of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: You are referring to the conversation with the gentleman who questioned me, the gentleman with whom I spoke?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mark a map for that person?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I marked a map, but it wasn't a map of the town. It was a map of Dobrinja, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you signed the map that you marked is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, may I proffer to the witness the Exhibit P3232.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is a map of Dobrinja which you marked, is it?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could that map be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have no ELMO on our screen under the video evidence button, as far as I can see. Now I have nothing on my screen any more. None of the buttons...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is slowly resuming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says -- on the video evidence, it says "no signal" so there must be something.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It can be viewed on the video channel now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map, you have video mark circled in certain places and put numbers inside those circle?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I have marked certain locations and numbers in the circles. There are numbers in the circle and I have marked these places with these numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we start from the last number and go backwards. At number 5, where you have marked "5" beside a dot, what does the dot indicate?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: That is the place from which they opened sniper fire. It is by that street. So there was a stronghold there and we all knew that they would shoot from there. So it was in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you say what the dot beside the circled number 4 indicates?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: It indicates the place where this girl had been wounded, the girl that we have already spoken about. So it was more or less at that site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have marked a spot number 3 or you have put a number 3 beside a dot on the map. What does this dot indicate?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: This indicates the location of my flat and the place where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have marked on your map -- on this map, a number 2 beside a dot. Could you say what that indicates?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not sure this time, but I think that just a minute ago the witness said that it was the flat in which he was earlier on when he spoke about his flat, and I think I heard the word "ranije," which means earlier on. So I don't know if we could ask this question once more to clarify the situation. Mr. President, I think that we should do this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, could you -- you heard that there were some questions as to the interpretation of the answer. Could you please try to clarify it from the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you go back to the dot beside the number 3 which you marked. What does that dot signify?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: That indicates the place where I was wounded, and that is the place where I lived, too. So I was wounded on the balcony on the third floor on the 4th of February, 1992. That is the date when that happened -- 1994, I apologise. That is when I was wounded in this massacre, when this massacre took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us now what the dot beside the number 2 signifies?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: That is the place where I was also wounded, where I was wounded in my head. That was the second time I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The 13th, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the building you said that you would have to enter Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. from the back, from holes created in the back of the building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You would enter from the back and the dot indicates the place where I was wounded. So that flat was facing the street from which it was impossible to enter. That is where there was sniper shooting and it is also from the direction where the girl was wounded. So, yes, we would enter the building from the rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is a dot that you have marked here with a circled number 1 beside it. What does that dot signify?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Dot number 1 indicates the place where I was wounded the first time. So on the 24th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at the dot beside the circled number 3. That dot is the area towards the back of the building in which you lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The street to the front of that building would be Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the front side, and I lived in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva number 5. That is -- that's the entrance, if I have understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You may remove the document. With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, I respectfully request that the witness be shown a photograph marked P3678B. Actually, it is a Quicktime movie, 360-degree Quicktime movie. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see anything on your screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I see that there is no broadcast. We have a nice picture of this courtroom without anyone in it. Yes, it is on our screen now, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We are going to look right around at the totality of this photograph and then I will ask you a couple of questions. Can we just go around slowly ending back to where we begin. To the right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a fair reproduction of the area behind your apartment building with the asphalted playground?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the background of the picture, or just immediately beyond the asphalted playground, do you see a structure there going across that area just beyond the asphalted playground?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please. I don't think I have understood it well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just beyond the asphalted playground, going across the middle of the screen, do you see a structure there? Can you say what it is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see a building. I don't really understand. I don't know what it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will have the picture focused a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you turn slightly to the right please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there is a structure going right across the middle of the screen from left to right. Can you identify that structure?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the asphalted surface in the foreground of this picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this question has been asked three times now and I think that it is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. I think that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we will hear it for a fourth time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- witness did not specifically answer to the question as far as I understand the question. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the asphalted playground in the foreground of the picture?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And beyond that towards the middle of the picture and to the left, do you see a motor car?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately above that motor car, do you see a structure that goes from the left of the picture right across the middle to the right of the picture?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: The structure is a car park, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would you turn the picture a little bit to the left, please. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify this building that you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It is the building I lived in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you locate the balcony that you were at when you were injured?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. But could you move this photograph a bit to the right for me to be certain. It will be clearer. It will be more visible then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will do so and can you tell us when to stop?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: That is fine there. You don't have to go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your apartment or the balcony that you were on, there?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe where it is?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether you can see what I am pointing to. If you can, I will point to it. Otherwise, I will explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is it technically possible that your case manager moves the tiny little circle over the screen without changing the picture so that the witness could guide you and say, "a bit more to the left," "a bit more upwards"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think that is not only technically possible, it is an excellent way of getting to what I am trying to accomplish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a moving cursor on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just direct us whether to the left or to the right or upwards or downwards to your apartment.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you move the cursor to the right. It is on the same floor, but move it to the right. It is the next balcony. Could you put it down just a bit. That is the flat in which I lived and that is the balcony which I have spoken about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But now I am afraid that you have to describe where this is, Mr. Stamp, so the problem is now yours. But if I could assist you, I can easily --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am grateful for the assistance. I was going to make an effort myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the screen, there are five rows of balconies. The one most at the right has one parabolic antenna second from below. Next one has two parabolic antennas, one below, one, two storeys higher, and then the next row which is hidden half, that means that only two balconies are visible beyond the tree, it is the lower one of these two balconies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am very grateful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to assist you all by concluding by tomorrow or Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And we are indeed making more progress than I expected. Thank you very much, Mr. President. Thank you. The photograph may be removed from the screen. Finally, there is an exhibit, I think it is D64, which I would like to recall and have just a small portion of that shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you rewind to the start of that video, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a quick rewind button on this machine?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am wondering, if my friends do not object, if I can conclude provisionally the examination-in-chief now and locate what is just two minutes, if that much, of video and perhaps just have him identify a particular area and answer two questions. I don't know if that would be objected to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you mind, Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if Mr. Stamp would just do this part of the examination-in-chief after he has selected a very short portion of the video because otherwise it might take quite some time to locate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may answer, we could perhaps leave two or three minutes to the Prosecution team in order to find this part and then perhaps in five minutes' time, they could continue with this series of question because I think that would be a lot more reasonable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it is just one or two -- just a couple of questions or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just approximately three or four questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think it would take you to locate the specific part of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It would probably take a couple of minutes but I don't want to have the courtroom remaining idle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know, Mr. Stamp, but as you may have noticed, discussing these issues takes approximately just as long as the time we would have to wait for you. Perhaps if you could assist the technicians, I would easily leave you to go out of the courtroom to detect it very quickly with the technicians or do it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we proceed with the video from the start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I lost my signal, but I believe it is on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is again -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop there, please, and go back to the start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that video which you just saw a fair and accurate reproduction of the scene behind your apartment, at a place behind your apartment on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is what we were able to see just before the end of the tape, that is the location where the third shell impacted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you see on that tape someone coming from a window of that building?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and play the tape once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you rewind it to the beginning and play that portion again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what was your question, please? What is it that you are interested in while we are waiting for the tape?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to see exactly where somebody comes from the building and then I will ask you a couple of questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this the beginning of the portion or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is the beginning. It is about to be played back, I take it. Please proceed with the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say why persons would exit the building from that place?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We exited through this side of the building because the other side was exposed to sniper fire, that exactly the direction that I mentioned, that I indicated on the map. You could also see the stairs which were partly damaged with the shell. So this would be one of the exits that I talked about. This is what we used to get out into the building, depending on where you live. People left the building through those small openings, small windows, because on the other side of the building, there was sniper fire. It was not possible to get out on that side of the building because you would soon be hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that sniper fire that you speak of from the other side of the building is the sniper fire that came down the street from the area on the map which you marked number 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, Mr. President, that concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Hafizovic, you will now be examined by Defence counsel. Is it you, Ms. Pilipovic, or you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, who will cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Me, Your Honour. Thank you very much. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. I should like to ask you several question which we will take up in order. Very well. Witness, would you tell the Chamber what was the situation like with the lines of conflict between the two parties during the war? Would you precisely indicate to the Chamber where they were.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I am afraid I don't quite understand your question. But I think I can answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you haven't understood it, I will rephrase it. Can you tell us, Witness, what you knew about the position of the separation lines between the two belligerent parties?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you about the position of these lines, but all of us who lived there knew very well where it was possible for us to move and where it was not, if that is what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So I presume you also knew where you shouldn't be venturing?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because we didn't dare because of the shooting. The same goes for the street that I talked about. As soon as you venture into that street, you risked being killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are referring -- you could hear the people who were close to the front line?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about the areas which were close to the front line, that is, in the vicinity of the separation line which opposed the two parties to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was referring to the area where the lines were, that is, the area where we dare move, where we would walk. So there were such areas where it was not possible to move freely, although they were actually free because of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. If there were free areas, that is areas where you could move, could you indicate on the map for us where was the area where you didn't dare go?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I could indicate some such areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I know that during the relevant times you were 17, relatively young. Therefore, what do you know about the locations of the command post of the brigade which was located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I was a civilian. I was not a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know, sir, that you were a civilian, but that was not my question. I wanted to know whether you knew where the command post of the brigade which was located in Dobrinja was? Just tell us yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. Would it be possible for you to rephrase the question? I am not quite clear as to what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the question seems quite clear to me. Did you know where the command posts of the brigade located in Dobrinja were?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: No. Well, actually, I know where it was located, but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you know where they were located, can you indicate those locations for us? Can you tell us where they were?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: Dobrinja II.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry, we didn't hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the English booth tells me that they couldn't hear you. I think that was when you asked whether the witness knows where they were located, whether he could indicate those locations and whether he could tell us where they were, I think that is the part the English booth might have missed. The answer was "Dobrinja II," so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my apologies to the English chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Where was the command post of the brigade located in Dobrinja? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honour, whether you intend to finish at a quarter to 2.00 or 2.00. Just a practical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... because this courtroom will be used this afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will find the suitable moment to break. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where other command posts were located? I am referring to the battalions, not the brigade, but the battalions that were located in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I am able to tell you such locations. I don't know those streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me just now that you didn't know the street where they were, but would you be able to indicate approximately where they were on a map?

utterances.speaker: ELDAR HAFIZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I have anything to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking you whether you have anything to do with that or not, I am just trying to find out whether you are able to indicate such locations or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Hafizovic, the relevance of the questions put to you and whether you think that you have got something to do with those subjects touched upon by the questions, you can leave it to us. If you have any specific problem with it, please tell me, and if not, you just answer the question. Sometimes you might not perfectly perceive why it is relevant for the Defence, but we will keep a close eye on that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that we should perhaps let the witness think about the question. We can stop here and I will continue with the same line of questioning tomorrow when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hafizovic, we cannot continue this afternoon since this courtroom is used for another case this afternoon. That means that we resume tomorrow morning in the same courtroom at 9.00. And that is a message for everyone. We adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
